Brown Soda Bread with Salted Butter

Served at: Feast of St. Muirgen (Lí Ban the Mermaid)

Serves 6-8Prep 15 minCook 45 min

On the Feast of St. Muirgen, also known as Lí Ban the Mermaid, this hearty Brown Soda Bread with Salted Butter is a traditional offering, symbolizing the simple, nourishing bounty of the land and sea. Its rustic charm and wholesome ingredients evoke the ancient Irish shores where Lí Ban once swam, providing sustenance and comfort to those gathered in celebration. Served warm with a generous smear of salted butter, it's a taste of heritage and myth.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (240g) whole wheat flour
  • 1 1/2 cups (180g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1 3/4 cups (420ml) buttermilk
  • 4 tablespoons (56g) salted butter, softened, for serving

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Lightly flour a baking sheet or line with parchment paper.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, all-purpose flour, baking soda, and salt until well combined.
  3. Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and pour in the buttermilk.
  4. Using a wooden spoon or your hands, gently mix the ingredients until just combined. Be careful not to overmix; the dough should be soft and shaggy.
  5. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Gently shape it into a round loaf, about 1 1/2 to 2 inches (4-5 cm) thick. Do not knead it excessively.
  6. Transfer the loaf to the prepared baking sheet.
  7. Using a sharp knife, score a deep cross into the top of the loaf, extending almost to the edges. This helps the bread cook evenly and is traditionally said to let the 'fairies out'.
  8. Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom. If it's browning too quickly, you can loosely tent it with foil.
  9. Remove the bread from the oven and transfer it to a wire rack to cool slightly.
  10. Serve warm, sliced, with generous amounts of softened salted butter.

Tips

  • Do not overmix the dough; overworking it will result in a tough bread. Mix just until the ingredients come together.
  • If you don't have buttermilk, you can make a substitute by adding 1 tablespoon of lemon juice or white vinegar to a liquid measuring cup, then filling the rest with regular milk to 1 3/4 cups (420ml). Let it sit for 5 minutes before using.
  • For an extra rustic touch, sprinkle a tablespoon of oats over the top of the loaf before baking.
